# Why Érōs is spelled that way — and what it costs to get it right

There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *eros*. This is the file on how **Érōs** replaced it.

Érōs stands at the beginning in Hesiod and at the margins in Homer. He is one of the oldest gods, yet his stories are few — because his power is everywhere.

## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Érōs
- **ASCII form:** eros
- **Meaning:** "Love, desire (from ἔραμαι)"
- **Domain of influence:** Love, Desire, Attraction
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** Ἔρως
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 122 of 437

## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Ἔρως**, as LSJ and Beekes record. On the evidence, it means "Love, desire (from ἔραμαι)".

Strip **Érōs** to *eros* and 2 pieces of evidence vanish:

- **e → É** — Epsilon with acute: the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.
- **o → ō** — Omega: long omicron: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.

Spoken, the name runs `/ˈe.rɔːs/` — "EH-ross" — the accent falls on the first syllable; the o of the second is held longer than English allows, deep and sustained.

## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Érōs** lives at [/eros/](/eros/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/eros/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/eros/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/eros/patterns/).

Tier-1 is not a compliment; it is a measurement. This restoration keeps something the ASCII form provably loses, and the measurement is repeatable.

## Where the Name Stood First

Numerous red-figure and black-figure vases depict Eros as a winged youth or child; the so-called Erotes appear on wedding vessels and funerary reliefs. No major sanctuary, but the Erotes were honored in gymnasia and private devotion. The temple on the web is the newest of these addresses — the first one that fits in a pocket.

## The Archetype at Work

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) seats this temple in **4 industries**, each match argued and weighted: **Love, Dating & Relationships** (desire itself; the arrow in every match.); **Beauty, Fashion & Cosmetics** (desire as the engine of attraction marketing.); **Mental Health & Emotional Wellness** (freud made Eros the name of the life drive; psychoanalysis runs on his energy.). The [Resonance File](/eros/blog/resonance/) reads those seats through the myths themselves.

The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on.
